content.comment_body: I have two [product_name] devices communicating with each other, but one suddenly stopped responding. I can still communicate with the other unit. Firmware version is [version_no]. The RX/TX LED remains steady orange and the LINK LED is steady green. Device IP: 172.26.2.224, computer IP: 172.26.2.200. The device does not reply to ping. It's able to run its program using the SD card. This is the second device where this issue has occurred. Both [product_name] units are unable to communicate.
Hello [user_name], You can find an example of communication for [product_name] devices here: [document]

Hi, 1. Verify your IP settings. Each PC and device on the network must have a unique IP address. After performing downloads, the IP address of a [product_name] may change. If a new IP matches another device on the network, an address conflict occurs and ping requests will not be answered. Connect one [product_name], check its IP and try to ping it. Then check the second device’s IP, change if needed, and ping the second unit. Once both are configured with different IPs, both should reply to ping. Hope this helps.

Thanks for your suggestion. The program ran fine until communication stopped; it still works with other [product_name] units. I have changed the IP on the affected [product_name] several times. I always test the new IP with a ping to ensure no conflicts before updating the device. There is no ping response from two different PCs. With the same cable, I can ping other [product_name] devices. Direct connection without a network switch also fails. The Link LED is always on. Could it be that the IP shown is not the one actually being used? Is there a way to completely reset the [product_name], or reload the firmware like with [version_no] controllers?

We have encountered a new problem and a possible cause. In the application that failed previously, we installed a new [product_name], replacing the units that stopped working. The new unit is communicating very slowly—sometimes signal transfer takes up to 3 seconds. The Link LED stays green even with no cable connected. We discovered that moving the power supply (for the [product_name]) 10cm away resolves the issue temporarily and restores normal communication, with the Link LED functioning properly. However, the previous devices affected by this issue continue to not work, even after several days disconnected and with their power supply 15cm away. All devices are [product_name] models, powered by a 24VDC supply.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report sudden, unexplained communication failures between [product_name] modules, even after successful operation and repeated troubleshooting. Issues persist despite network reconfiguration, changes in cabling, bypassing switches, and replacing devices. Additionally, the physical location of the power supply relative to the [product_name] hardware appears to impact communication stability, suggesting possible hardware sensitivity or electrical interference.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] modules to maintain reliable communication, support secure IP configuration, and offer recovery options such as a complete reset or firmware reload, similar to features available in other [company_name] controllers.
